# Incident Report: MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.1.21.58 |
| MAC address | 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2 (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-ES9F3ML |
| NetBIOS/AD domain | WIN11OFFICE (Kerberos realm WIN11OFFICE.COM) |
| Logged-in user | gwyatt (Kerberos CNameString `gwyatt`, realm WIN11OFFICE.COM, confirmed in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic to DC 10.1.21.2) |
| LAN | 10.1.21.0/24, DHCP-assigned by 10.1.21.1, domain controller at 10.1.21.2 |

AD chatter (samr/lsarpc/drsuapi, ~3,588 exchanges) is exclusively between 10.1.21.58 and the domain controller 10.1.21.2 — standard Group Policy/authentication background traffic, not lateral movement. No other internal host was targeted.

## 2. Malware Family

**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No IDS/Suricata alerts or AV detections were provided alongside the pcap, and the payload itself transferred entirely inside TLS, so no file could be carved and hashed or matched to a known family signature.

The observed traffic pattern is a **ClickFix/fake-file-host malvertising delivery chain** consistent with a commodity Windows loader or infostealer:

1. `hiyter.com` — initial landing/redirector (t+45.35s)
2. `media.megafilehub4.lat` — fake file-hosting front (t+45.92s)
3. `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` — served a 16 MB file to the host over TLS (t+48.37s, single TCP session, 11,470 frames inbound vs 8,252 outbound — clearly a download, not a normal page load)
4. Post-execution, the host began calling out with a machine ID and token to a **browser-fingerprinting/check-in gate at whitepepper.su**, alternating a scripted `agent=Chrome` then `agent=Edge` user-agent string within 8 seconds — automated, not human browsing
5. The gate response repeatedly read `cant open archive 172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bda042ad17a1.zip`, indicating server-side per-victim archive staging that failed to deliver
6. Two further Cloudflare-fronted domains (`holiday-forever.cc`, `communicationfirewall-security.cc`) were then contacted over TLS, each delivering ~100-120 KB inbound (secondary payload/config retrieval)

This TTP chain (fake file-host → oversized single download → JS fingerprint/check-in gate with ID+token → secondary TLS fetches) is the standard delivery pattern for commodity stealer/loader campaigns. Exact family name cannot be stated with confidence from network evidence alone.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### C2 / infrastructure domains and endpoints (IP:port)
| Domain | Resolved IP(s) | Port(s) | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| hiyter.com | 104.21.22.231, 172.67.207.145 | 443 | Landing/redirector |
| media.megafilehub4.lat | 104.21.48.156, 172.67.154.67 | 443 | Fake file host |
| arch.filemegahab4.sbs | 104.21.46.67, 172.67.136.13 | 443 | Payload delivery (16 MB, TLS-encrypted) |
| whooptm.cyou | 62.72.32.156 | 443 | Redirector/gate |
| whitepepper.su | 153.92.1.49 | 80, 443 | Fingerprint/check-in gate (cleartext HTTP) |
| holiday-forever.cc | 80.97.160.24 | 443 | Secondary TLS fetch |
| communicationfirewall-security.cc | 104.21.9.36, 172.67.141.109 | 443 | Secondary TLS fetch |

Note: the `.sbs`, `.lat`, `.cc`, `.cyou`, and one `.su` domain sit behind Cloudflare shared IPs — the IP addresses themselves are not unique attacker infrastructure, the domains/SNI values are the actionable indicator.

### Malicious URLs (observed in cleartext HTTP)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`
- `http://whitepepper.su/favicon.ico`

### Malware/campaign identifiers
- Bot/victim ID: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`
- C2 token: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`
- Referenced archive filename (server-side, victim-specific, from gate error page): `172.56.88.98-038485b1855ec7a1ba5bda042ad17a1.zip`

### File hashes
**None obtainable.** The 16 MB payload transfer from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` and all traffic to `holiday-forever.cc` / `communicationfirewall-security.cc` occurred entirely inside TLS. No HTTP object could be exported (`tshark --export-objects http` returned nothing beyond benign Microsoft/Google traffic), and no filename, Content-Disposition header, or hash string appears anywhere in cleartext in this capture. Do not treat the 32-hex-character string in the archive filename above as a SHA256 — it is not full-length SHA256 (64 hex chars) and its exact meaning (session/fingerprint hash vs file hash) cannot be determined from network evidence alone.

## 4. Summary

DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (10.1.21.58, user gwyatt) was lured through a chain of typosquat "file host" domains, downloaded a 16 MB file over TLS from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`, then began automated check-in traffic (spoofed Chrome/Edge user-agents, ID+token parameters) to a fingerprinting gate at `whitepepper.su`, followed by TLS calls to two more attacker-controlled domains. This is consistent with a fake-file-host/ClickFix-style loader or stealer infection. No lateral movement or additional internal victims were observed. Family attribution is behavioral only; recommend submitting the domain list above to endpoint/AV tooling with local telemetry (process tree, file system, registry) to confirm the specific malware family, since network evidence alone cannot yield a file hash here.
